Summarise how housing markets fell and recovered around the 2008 crisis

crisis_recovery.Rd

For each market area, finds the highest yearly level before the crisis (2000-2006), the lowest yearly level during the downturn (2007-2010), how far the area fell between the two, and the first later year in which it returned to its pre-crisis peak.

Usage

crisis_recovery(data = tx_housing_markets, measure = "sales", areas = NULL)

Arguments

data

A data frame with the same columns as tx_housing_markets. Defaults to tx_housing_markets.

measure

The measure to summarise: "sales" (number of homes sold), "median_real" (median sale price in July 2015 dollars) or "median" (median sale price, not adjusted for inflation).

areas

Optional character vector of area names to include. Defaults to all areas in data.

Value

A tibble with one row per area and the columns:

area

Market area.

measure

The measure summarised.

peak_year, peak

Year and level of the pre-crisis peak.

low_year, low

Year and level of the downturn low.

drop_pct

Percentage change from peak to low. Negative values mean the area fell.

recovery_year

First year after the low in which the level was back at or above the pre-crisis peak, or NA if this did not happen.

years_to_recover

Years from the low to recovery, or NA.

status

"Recovered", "Not recovered by 2015", "Never fell below peak" or "Insufficient data".

Details

Each year's level is the average of the available monthly values in that year. Using averages rather than totals means years with missing months, and the partial year 2015 (January to July), can still be compared with full years. Because 2015 only covers the first seven months, its average may differ slightly from a full-year figure due to seasonal patterns.

Examples

crisis_recovery(measure = "sales", areas = c("Austin", "Dallas", "Houston")) |>
  dplyr::select(area, drop_pct, recovery_year, status)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>   area    drop_pct recovery_year status               
#>   <chr>      <dbl>         <int> <chr>                
#> 1 Austin     -34.4          2013 Recovered            
#> 2 Dallas     -34              NA Not recovered by 2015
#> 3 Houston    -29.9          2014 Recovered            
# How far home sales fell in three large markets, and whether they recovered

crisis_recovery(measure = "median_real") |>
  dplyr::slice_min(drop_pct, n = 5) |>
  dplyr::select(area, peak_year, low_year, drop_pct, status)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 5
#>   area        peak_year low_year drop_pct status               
#>   <chr>           <int>    <int>    <dbl> <chr>                
#> 1 Galveston        2006     2009    -32.3 Not recovered by 2015
#> 2 Garland          2002     2010    -27.8 Not recovered by 2015
#> 3 Brownsville      2005     2009    -20.6 Not recovered by 2015
#> 4 Laredo           2004     2010    -19.8 Not recovered by 2015
#> 5 Harlingen        2000     2010    -19.7 Not recovered by 2015
# The five areas with the biggest fall in inflation-adjusted prices
